【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),
(power:TEXT, : The power of the card.-∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(printings:TEXT, : A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.-),
(promoTypes:TEXT, promo Types: A list of promotional types for a card.-"arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork", Examples: [boxtopper,boosterfun, boosterfun, release,buyabox]),
(purchaseUrls:TEXT, purchase Urls: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.-),
(rarity:TEXT, : The card printing rarity.-, Examples: [uncommon, common, rare]),
(scryfallId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [7a5cd03c-4227-4551-aa4b-7d119f0468b5]),
(scryfallIllustrationId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [be2f7173-c8b7-4172-a388-9b2c6b3c16e5]),
(scryfallOracleId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [fc2ccab7-cab1-4463-b73d-898070136d74]),
(setCode:TEXT, Set Code: The set printing code that the card is from.-, Examples: [10E, 2ED, 2XM]),
(side:TEXT, : The identifier of the card side.-Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card., Examples: [a, b, c]),
(subtypes:TEXT, : A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.-, Examples: [Human,Cleric, Angel, Bird,Soldier]),
(supertypes:TEXT, super types: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash.-list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes, Examples: [Legendary, Basic, Legendary,Snow]),
(tcgplayerProductId:TEXT, tcg player ProductId: -, Examples: [15032, 15033, 15045]),
(text:TEXT, : The rules text of the card.-),
(toughness:TEXT, : The toughness of the card.-, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(type:TEXT, : The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes.-"Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant", Examples: [Creature — Human Cleric]),
(types:TEXT, : A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.-, Examples: [Creature, Instant, Enchantment]),
(uuid:TEXT, : The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.-, Examples: [00010d56-fe38-5e35-8aed-518019aa36a5]),
(variations:TEXT, : -, Examples: [b7c19924-b4bf-56fc-aa73-f586e940bd42]),
(watermark:TEXT, : The name of the watermark on the card.-, Examples: [set (HOU), set (LGN), set (ONS)])
]
# Table: foreign_data
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id number identifying this row of data-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The foreign flavor text of the card.-),
(language:TEXT, : The foreign language of card.-, Examples: [German, Spanish, French]),

(uuid:TEXT, : -, Examples: [5f8287b1-5bb6-5f4c-ad17-316a40d5bb0c])
]

]

【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),
(power:TEXT, : The power of the card.-∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(printings:TEXT, : A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.-),
(promoTypes:TEXT, promo Types: A list of promotional types for a card.-"arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork", Examples: [boxtopper,boosterfun, boosterfun, release,buyabox]),
(purchaseUrls:TEXT, purchase Urls: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.-),
(rarity:TEXT, : The card printing rarity.-, Examples: [uncommon, common, rare]),
(scryfallId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [7a5cd03c-4227-4551-aa4b-7d119f0468b5]),
(scryfallIllustrationId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [be2f7173-c8b7-4172-a388-9b2c6b3c16e5]),
(scryfallOracleId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [fc2ccab7-cab1-4463-b73d-898070136d74]),
(setCode:TEXT, Set Code: The set printing code that the card is from.-, Examples: [10E, 2ED, 2XM]),
(side:TEXT, : The identifier of the card side.-Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card., Examples: [a, b, c]),
(subtypes:TEXT, : A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.-, Examples: [Human,Cleric, Angel, Bird,Soldier]),
(supertypes:TEXT, super types: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash.-list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes, Examples: [Legendary, Basic, Legendary,Snow]),
(tcgplayerProductId:TEXT, tcg player ProductId: -, Examples: [15032, 15033, 15045]),
(text:TEXT, : The rules text of the card.-),
(toughness:TEXT, : The toughness of the card.-, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(type:TEXT, : The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes.-"Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant", Examples: [Creature — Human Cleric]),

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to find the release date of the set containing the card 'Ancestor's Chosen'. This involves identifying the card, finding the set it belongs to, and then retrieving the set's release information. The 'name' column helps identify the card. I don't see release date in the schema, so I cannot answer the question.

The question asks for the release date of a set of cards named 'Ancestor's Chosen'. The hint indicates that 'Ancestor's Chosen' refers to the `name` column in the `cards` table and that the release date is found in the `releaseDate` column. However, looking at the schema, there is no `releaseDate` column directly in the `cards` table. The `rulings` table has a `date` column, which might represent a release date or a ruling date. The `set_translations` table has a `translation` column and `language` column, and it links to the `sets` table via `setCode`. The `sets` table has columns like `booster`, `isFoilOnly`, etc., but no direct release date. The `cards` table contains the `name` of the card. Since the question is about the *set* of cards and the hint mentions 'Ancestor's Chosen' as a card name, and the `cards` table has the `name` column, I will need to use `cards.name` to filter for the specific card. The question asks 'When was the set of cards... released?', which implies we need a date associated with the set. The `rulings` table has a `date` column, and it's linked to `cards` via `uuid`. It's possible this `date` in `rulings` is the closest we have to a release date for a card's set. Therefore, I will select `cards.name` to filter for 'Ancestor's Chosen' and `rulings.date` to find the release date. The `uuid` column is necessary to join `cards` and `rulings` tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.releaseDate FROM sets AS T1 WHERE T1.code = (SELECT T2.setCode FROM cards AS T2 WHERE T2.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen')

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter cards by set name 'Coldsnap', 2) Filter cards with converted mana cost greater than 5, 3) Filter cards with unknown power ('*'), 4) Count the cards. The name column is needed to filter by the set name. The convertedManaCost column is needed to filter by converted mana cost. The power column is needed to filter cards with unknown power. The sets table is needed to join with the cards table to filter by set name.

The question asks to count cards from a specific set ('Coldsnap') that have a converted mana cost greater than 5 and an unknown power. Therefore, I need to access the `cards` table to filter by `convertedManaCost` and `power`, and I need to join it with the `sets` table to filter by the set name 'Coldsnap'. The `sets.name` column is needed to identify the set 'Coldsnap'. The `cards.convertedManaCost` column is needed to filter for costs greater than 5. The `cards.power` column is needed to identify cards with unknown power. The `cards.uuid` and `sets.code` columns are needed to join the `cards` and `sets` tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T1.setCode = T2.code WHERE T1.convertedManaCost > 5 AND T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND (T1.power = '*' OR T1.power IS NULL)

Therefore, I need to access the `cards` table to filter by `convertedManaCost` and `power`, and I need to join it with the `sets` table to filter by the set name 'Coldsnap'. The `sets.name` column is needed to identify the set 'Coldsnap'. The `cards.convertedManaCost` column is needed to filter for costs greater than 5. The `cards.power` column is needed to identify cards with unknown power. The `cards.uuid` and `sets.code` columns are needed to join the `cards` and `sets` tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T1.setCode = T2.code WHERE T1.convertedManaCost > 5 AND T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND (T1.power = '*' OR T1.power IS NULL)

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the set named 'Coldsnap', 2) Identify the Italian translation, 3) Retrieve the text ruling in Italian for all cards in that set. The set name and language are needed for filtering. The text ruling is needed for the final result. The tables need to be joined using the foreign keys.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.text FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap'

SELECT T1.text
FROM foreign_data AS T1
WHERE T1.language = 'Italian'
AND T1.uuid IN (SELECT uuid FROM cards WHERE setCode = (SELECT code FROM sets WHERE name = 'Coldsnap'));

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for the set named 'Coldsnap', 2) Find the cards in that set with the highest faceConvertedManaCost, 3) Filter for Italian translations of these cards, and 4) Retrieve the Italian names. The set name is needed to filter the cards. The faceConvertedManaCost is needed to find the highest mana cost. The language is needed to filter for Italian. The translation is needed to retrieve the Italian names. The cards table is connected to the other tables through the uuid.

The question asks for the Italian names of cards from the 'Coldsnap' set with the highest converted mana cost. This requires joining the 'sets' table to filter by the set name 'Coldsnap' and the 'set_translations' table to filter by language 'Italian' and retrieve the translated name. The 'cards' table is needed to filter by the highest 'faceConvertedManaCost' and to link to the 'set_translations' table via 'cardKingdomId' (assuming 'cardKingdomId' in 'cards' corresponds to 'setCode' in 'sets' or a related key for joining). However, the schema shows `set_translations.setCode` referencing `sets.code`. Therefore, we need to join `sets` and `set_translations` to get the Italian translation for cards within the 'Coldsnap' set. To find the cards with the highest converted mana cost, we need the `faceConvertedManaCost` from the `cards` table. The `cardKingdomId` in `cards` likely links to the `code` in `sets` to associate cards with their sets. Since we need the Italian name and the set name, we'll need `sets.name` and `set_translations.translation` and `set_translations.language`. We also need `cards.faceConvertedManaCost` and `cards.cardKingdomId` to link to the set and find the highest mana cost. The example for `sets.name` includes 'Coldsnap', and `set_translations.language` includes 'Italian'. The example for `cards.faceConvertedManaCost` would be numerical values, allowing us to find the maximum.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T4 INNER JOIN sets AS T5 ON T4.setCode = T5.code WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap')

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT MAX(T4.faceConvertedManaCost)
        FROM cards AS T4
        INNER JOIN sets AS T5
          ON T4.setCode = T5.code
        WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap'

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T3.translation
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN sets AS T2
  ON T1.cardKingdomId = T2.code
INNER JOIN set_translations AS T3
  ON T2.code = T3.setCode
WHERE
  T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T3.language = 'Italian' AND T1.faceConvertedManaCost = (
    SELECT
      MAX(T_sub1.faceConvertedManaCost)
    FROM cards AS T_sub1
    INNER JOIN sets AS T_sub2
      ON T_sub1.cardKingdomId = T_sub2.code
    WHERE
      T_sub2.name = 'Coldsnap'
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for cards that do not have multiple faces (otherFaceIds IS NULL), 2) Find the card with the highest faceConvertedManaCost, 3) Retrieve the artist for that card. The artist column is needed to retrieve the illustrator's name. The faceConvertedManaCost column is needed to find the card with the highest mana cost. The otherFaceIds column is needed to filter the cards without multiple faces.

The question asks for the artist of the card art with the highest converted mana cost, among cards that do not have multiple faces. The 'artist' column in the 'cards' table is needed to identify the illustrator. The 'faceConvertedManaCost' column in the 'cards' table is needed to find the card with the highest cost. The 'otherFaceIds' column in the 'cards' table is needed to filter for cards that do not have multiple faces, as indicated by the hint 'doesn't have multiple faces refers to side IS NULL' (although 'side' is not a column, 'otherFaceIds' being NULL or empty would imply no other faces). The 'uuid' column is needed to join the 'cards' and 'rulings' tables if we were to consider rulings, but the question only asks about card art and cost, not rulings.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT artist FROM cards WHERE side IS NULL ORDER BY convertedManaCost DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

The 'otherFaceIds' column in the 'cards' table is needed to filter for cards that do not have multiple faces, as indicated by the hint 'doesn't have multiple faces refers to side IS NULL' (although 'side' is not a column, 'otherFaceIds' being NULL or empty would imply no other faces). The 'uuid' column is needed to join the 'cards' and 'rulings' tables if we were to consider rulings, but the question only asks about card art and cost, not rulings.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT artist FROM cards WHERE otherFaceIds IS NULL OR otherFaceIds = '' ORDER BY faceConvertedManaCost DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the oldest card (based on release date). I also need to find the legal formats for that card. The `cards` table likely contains the release date and card information. The `legalities` table contains the legal formats. The `originalText` column is not relevant to the question.

The question asks for the release date of the oldest 'mythic' card and its legal play formats. To find the oldest card, I need a column that stores the release date. The hint mentions 'originalReleaseDate' and 'MIN(originalReleaseDate)', indicating this column is crucial for finding the oldest card. The question also specifies 'mythic card', which implies a column indicating rarity is needed. The hint confirms this with 'rarity = 'mythic''. Finally, the question asks for 'legal play formats', and the hint points to 'status = 'legal'' and 'format', suggesting these columns in the 'legalities' table are necessary. The 'cards' table likely contains the release date and rarity, while the 'legalities' table contains the format and status. Therefore, I need to join these tables on a common identifier, which is 'uuid' as indicated by the foreign key constraints.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.originalReleaseDate, T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.rarity = 'mythic' AND T1.originalReleaseDate = (SELECT MIN(originalReleaseDate) FROM cards WHERE rarity = 'mythic' AND originalReleaseDate IS NOT NULL) AND T2.status = 'Legal'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Count the number of cards illustrated by each artist, 2) Find the artist(s) with the minimum count, and 3) Retrieve the formats of play for those cards. The artist column is needed to group and count cards by illustrator. The format column is needed to list the formats of play. The tables cards and legalities are joined by the uuid.

The question asks to identify the illustrator who illustrated the least amount of cards and then list the formats of play for the cards they illustrated. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Count the number of cards illustrated by each artist from the 'cards' table. 2) Identify the artist with the minimum count. 3) Join the 'cards' table with the 'legalities' table using the 'uuid' to retrieve the 'format' of the cards illustrated by that artist. Therefore, the 'artist' column from 'cards' is needed to group and count illustrators. The 'uuid' column from 'cards' is needed to join with 'legalities'. The 'uuid' column from 'legalities' is needed to join with 'cards'. The 'format' column from 'legalities' is needed to list the formats of play.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist IN ( SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(id) = ( SELECT MIN(card_count) FROM ( SELECT COUNT(id) AS card_count FROM cards GROUP BY artist ) ) )

The `set_translations` table contains information about translations for sets, including the language and the translation itself. The `sets` table contains information about the sets, including their names. Therefore, I need to join `sets` and `set_translations` tables. I will filter `set_translations` for 'Korean' language to identify sets with Korean translations and for 'Japanese' language to identify sets without Japanese translations. The `name` column from the `sets` table is required to list the names of the sets.

The question asks for the display name of the parent ID for a child post with the highest score. This means I need to: 1. Identify child posts, which are posts where 'ParentId' is not null. 2. Find the child post with the maximum 'Score'. 3. Get the 'ParentId' of this highest-scoring child post. 4. Find the post that corresponds to this 'ParentId' (which will be the parent post). 5. Retrieve the 'OwnerDisplayName' of this parent post. Therefore, I need 'ParentId' and 'Score' from the 'posts' table to identify the child post and its score, and 'Id' and 'OwnerDisplayName' from the 'posts' table to identify the parent post and its display name.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.OwnerDisplayName FROM posts AS T1 INNER JOIN posts AS T2 ON T1.ParentId = T2.Id WHERE T1.Id = (SELECT Id FROM posts WHERE ParentId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY Score DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1)

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH TargetRaceId AS (
  -- Sub-question 1: Get the raceId for the '2008 Australian Grand Prix'.
  SELECT T1.raceId
  FROM races AS T1
  INNER JOIN circuits AS T2
    ON T1.circuitId = T2.circuitId
  WHERE
    T1.year = 2008 AND T2.circuitRef = 'australian'
), ChampionActualTime AS (
  -- Sub-question 2: Get the champion's actual time in seconds (T_champion_sec) for the identified raceId.
  SELECT
    (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 1, INSTR(T1.time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 3600) + -- Hours to seconds
    (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60) + -- Minutes to seconds
    (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') + INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1) AS REAL)) AS champion_time_sec -- Seconds (including milliseconds)
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRaceId AS TR
    ON T1.raceId = TR.raceId
  WHERE
    T1.time NOT LIKE '+%' AND T1.time IS NOT NULL -- Champion's time is in HH:MM:SS.mmm format
), AllActualTimes AS (
  -- Sub-question 3: Calculate the actual time in seconds for *all* drivers in the identified race who finished.
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN T1.time NOT LIKE '+%'
      THEN (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 1, INSTR(T1.time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 3600) + (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60) + (CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') + INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1) AS REAL))
      ELSE (SELECT champion_time_sec FROM ChampionActualTime) + CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 2) AS REAL)
    END AS actual_time_sec
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRaceId AS TR
    ON T1.raceId = TR.raceId
  WHERE
    T1.time IS NOT NULL -- Only consider drivers who finished the race
)
-- Main Question: Calculate the percentage difference.
SELECT
  (
    (MAX(actual_time_sec) - (SELECT champion_time_sec FROM ChampionActualTime)) * 100.0 / MAX(actual_time_sec)
  )
FROM AllActualTimes;

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T3.time
FROM circuits AS T1
INNER JOIN races AS T2
  ON T1.circuitId = T2.circuitId
INNER JOIN lapTimes AS T3
  ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId
WHERE
  T1.circuitRef = 'red_bull_ring'
ORDER BY
  CAST(SUBSTR(T3.time, 1, INSTR(T3.time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(T3.time, INSTR(T3.time, ':') + 1) AS REAL) ASC
LIMIT 1;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To determine the league with the most matches, I need to count the matches for each league and then find the maximum count. The League table provides the league name, and the Match table contains the league ID, which is used to link the matches to the leagues. The count of matches is based on the number of entries in the Match table for each league.

The question asks for the name of the league with the highest number of matches and the count of those matches. To achieve this, I need to join the 'League' table with the 'Match' table to link league names to match records. Then, I need to group the matches by league to count them and find the league with the maximum count. The 'League.name' column is needed to display the league's name. The 'Match.league_id' column is needed to link matches to leagues and to count the matches per league. The 'League.id' column is needed to join the 'League' and 'Match' tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.id) DESC LIMIT 1

The League table provides the league name, and the Match table contains the league ID, which is used to link the matches to the leagues. schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the name of the league with the highest number of matches and the count of those matches. To achieve this, I need to join the 'League' table with the 'Match' table to link league names to match records. Then, I need to group the matches by league to count them and find the league with the maximum count. The 'League.name' column is needed to display the league's name. The 'Match.league_id' column is needed to link matches to leagues and to count the matches per league. The 'League.id' column is needed to join the 'League' and 'Match' tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.league_id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.league_id) DESC LIMIT 1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the team_fifa_api_id of teams. I need to filter the teams based on their buildUpPlaySpeed, which should be between 51 and 59. The Team_Attributes table contains both the team_fifa_api_id and buildUpPlaySpeed.

The question asks for the `team_fifa_api_id` of teams that have a `buildUpPlaySpeed` between 50 and 60 (exclusive of 50, inclusive of 59 as per the hint's interpretation of 'more than 50 but less than 60'). The `Team_Attributes` table contains both `team_fifa_api_id` and `buildUpPlaySpeed`. Therefore, I need to select `team_fifa_api_id` from `Team_Attributes` and filter based on the `buildUpPlaySpeed` column.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT team_fifa_api_id FROM Team_Attributes WHERE buildUpPlaySpeed BETWEEN 51 AND 59

The team_long_name is needed to identify the teams. The buildUpPlayPassing is needed to filter for above-average values. The team_fifa_api_id is needed to join the tables and filter for the year. The date is needed to filter for the year.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT
      AVG(buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012. This requires joining the 'Team' table (for team names) with the 'Team_Attributes' table (for build-up play passing attributes). The hint specifies filtering by year 2012, which implies a date column is needed, although it's not explicitly provided in the schema. However, the hint mentions 'strftime('%Y', date) = '2012'', suggesting that the 'Match' table might contain a date column that can be used for filtering. The 'buildUpPlayPassing' column from 'Team_Attributes' is needed to calculate the average and filter for above-average values. The 'team_long_name' from the 'Team' table is the desired output.

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH TeamsPlayingIn2012 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT home_team_api_id AS team_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT away_team_api_id AS team_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
),
AvgBuildUpPassingFor2012Teams AS (
  SELECT AVG(TA.buildUpPlayPassing) AS avg_passing
  FROM Team_Attributes AS TA
  WHERE TA.team_api_id IN (SELECT team_id FROM TeamsPlayingIn2012)
    AND TA.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT DISTINCT T.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T
JOIN Team_Attributes AS TA
  ON T.team_api_id = TA.team_api_id
WHERE T.team_api_id IN (SELECT team_id FROM TeamsPlayingIn2012)

The player_name and height columns are needed to identify and filter the players. The heading_accuracy and player_fifa_api_id are needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is needed to group the heading_accuracy.

The question asks for the names of players whose heights are above 180 and to order them by their average heading accuracy in descending order. To achieve this, I need to access the player's name and height from the 'Player' table. The 'Player_Attributes' table contains the 'heading_accuracy' and 'player_fifa_api_id' which can be used to link back to the 'Player' table and calculate the average heading accuracy. The hint also explicitly mentions 'height > 180' and 'average heading accuracy = DIVIDE(SUM(heading_accuracy), COUNT(player_fifa_api_id))', confirming the need for these columns.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.player_name
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id
WHERE
  T1.height > 180
GROUP BY
  T1.player_name
ORDER BY
  AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

I will need to access the player names and their corresponding crossing scores. The Player table contains the player names, and the Player_Attributes table contains the crossing scores and the player_api_id which is used to link the two tables.

The question asks to identify the player who performs best in crossing actions among three specific players: Alexis, Ariel Borysiuk, and Arouna Kone. The 'best in crossing actions' is defined by the maximum 'crossing' value. Therefore, I need to find the 'player_name' from the 'Player' table and the 'crossing' attribute from the 'Player_Attributes' table. I will need to join these two tables on the player's API ID. The 'player_name' is needed to filter for the specific players mentioned in the question. The 'crossing' column is needed to determine who performs best. The 'player_fifa_api_id' is needed to link the player's name to their attributes.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.player_name IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone') ORDER BY T2.crossing DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

# Table: Player
[

[
(player_api_id:INTEGER, player api id: the id of the player api-, Examples: [505942, 155782, 162549]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, attacking work rate: the player's attacking work rate-commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low])
]

Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id

The Player table contains the player's name, and the Player_Attributes table contains the attacking work rate. Therefore, we need to join these tables to find the player names based on their attacking work rate.

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter patients by birth year 1937, 2) Filter for patients with total cholesterol above 250. The Birthday column is needed to filter by birth year. The T-CHO column is needed to filter by total cholesterol. The ID column is needed to link the tables.

The question asks to list patients born in 1937 with total cholesterol beyond the normal range. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Filter patients by their birth year (1937) from the 'Patient' table. 2. Filter laboratory results for 'T-CHO' greater than or equal to 250 from the 'Laboratory' table. 3. Join the 'Patient' and 'Laboratory' tables on the 'ID' column to link patient information with their laboratory results. The 'ID' column is essential for this join operation.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) = '1937' AND T2."T-CHO" >= 250

The question asks for the average anti-cardiolipin antibody (IgG) concentration for in-patients aged 50 and above. To determine this, I need to: 1. Identify patients who are in-patients using the 'Admission' column in the 'Patient' table. 2. Calculate the age of these patients using their 'Birthday' from the 'Patient' table and the current timestamp. 3. Filter for patients aged 50 and above. 4. Join the 'Patient' table with the 'Examination' table using the 'ID' column to access the 'aCL IgG' concentration. 5. Calculate the average of the 'aCL IgG' for the filtered patients. Therefore, the necessary columns are 'Admission' and 'Birthday' from the 'Patient' table, and 'ID' and 'aCL IgG' from the 'Examination' table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT AVG(T1.`aCL IgG`) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Patient AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.Admission = '+' AND (STRFTIME('%Y', 'now') - STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Birthday)) >= 50

  T1.ID,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(T2.ALP) = 0 THEN 'No Data'
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN T2.ALP >= 300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS ALP_Normal_Range
FROM Patient AS T1
LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS T2
  ON T1.ID = T2.ID
WHERE
  T1.Birthday = '1982-04-01'
GROUP BY
  T1.ID;

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.ID,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(T2.ALP) = 0 THEN 'No Data'
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN T2.ALP >= 300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS ALP_Normal_Range
FROM Patient AS T1
LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS T2
  ON T1.ID = T2.ID
WHERE
  T1.Birthday = '1982-04-01'
GROUP BY
  T1.ID;

The question asks for the name and location of events that have underspent their budget. To achieve this, I need to identify events and their associated budgets. The `event` table contains the `event_name` and `location`. The `budget` table contains information about the budget for each event, specifically the `remaining` amount. An event underspends its budget if the `remaining` amount is greater than 0. Therefore, I need to join the `event` and `budget` tables on `event_id` (implicitly through `link_to_event` in the `budget` table) and filter for budgets where `remaining > 0`. The `event_name` and `location` from the `event` table are the desired output, and `remaining` from the `budget` table is needed for filtering.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.event_name, T1.location FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event WHERE T2.remaining > 0

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Calculate the average parking cost, 2) Find events where the parking cost is less than the average. The event_name is needed to list the events. The budget table is needed to filter for parking costs and link to the event. The expense table is needed to get the cost. The link_to_event column is needed to link the tables.

The question asks for event names with less than the average parking cost. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Identify expenses related to parking. This requires the 'category' column from the 'budget' table. 2. Calculate the total cost of parking expenses. This requires the 'cost' column from the 'expense' table. 3. Count the number of parking expenses to determine the average. This also requires the 'cost' column from the 'expense' table. 4. Link expenses to budgets to filter by 'Parking' category. This requires 'link_to_budget' from 'expense' and 'budget_id' from 'budget'. 5. Link budgets to events to get the event names. This requires 'link_to_event' from 'budget' and 'event_id' from 'event'. 6. Retrieve the 'event_name' from the 'event' table. The hint mentions 'event_id' in the context of calculating the average, which implies we need to count distinct events associated with parking expenses. However, the 'expense' table has 'expense_id' and 'link_to_budget', and the 'budget' table has 'budget_id' and 'link_to_event'. The foreign key in 'budget' is 'link_to_event' which references 'event.event_id'. So, to get the event name, I need to join 'expense' with 'budget' and then with 'event'. The average cost calculation needs to be done on parking expenses. The hint's `COUNT(event_id)` is a bit ambiguous given the schema, but it likely refers to counting the number of parking expenses or the number of events that have parking expenses. Given the direct request for 'event_name', the 'event' table is necessary. The 'budget' table is needed to filter by category 'Parking' and to link expenses to events. The 'expense' table is needed for the cost of each expense and to link to the budget.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event WHERE T2.category = 'Parking' AND T2.spent < (SELECT avg(spent) FROM budget WHERE category = 'Parking')

The 'type' column in the 'event' table is needed to filter for game events. The 'cost' column in the 'expense' table is needed to calculate the total cost. The 'link_to_budget' in the 'expense' table is needed to link to the 'budget' table, and the 'link_to_event' in the 'budget' table is needed to link to the 'event' table. The question asks for the percentage of the cost for 'game' events. This requires calculating the total cost of all expenses related to game events and then dividing it by the total number of game events. The `event` table is needed to filter for events of type 'Game'. The `expense` table contains the `cost` information and is linked to the `budget` table, which in turn is linked to the `event` table. Therefore, I need to join `event` and `expense` (via `budget`) to get the cost associated with game events. The `type` column in the `event` table is used to filter for 'Game' events. The `cost` column in the `expense` table is used to sum up the costs. The `event_id` (implicitly from the foreign key `link_to_event` in `expense` and `budget` which links to `event`) is needed to count the number of game events.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT (SUM(T1.cost) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T3.event_id))
FROM expense AS T1
INNER JOIN budget AS T2
  ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id
INNER JOIN event AS T3
  ON T2.link_to_event = T3.event_id
WHERE T3.type = 'Game';

FROM yearmonth AS T1
